sections.h2: Filing a deed in Hillsdale County
sections.html:
Walk in to Room 212 of the County Office Building, 33 McCollum St., Hillsdale 49242, or phone (517) 437-2231. The window is staffed Monday to Friday from 8:30 in the morning until 5:00 in the afternoon. E-filings can be sent at any hour, but clerks work them only during posted hours and not on holidays.

Four e-recording vendors are approved: Indecomm, ePn, Simplifile and CSC/Ingeo. They are paid by ACH, may add charges of their own, and return the recorded document electronically. An e-filing that violates the Michigan Recording Act can be rejected.

A personal check will not pay for a paper filing, though certified funds are fine, meaning cashier's checks and money orders. Staff do not draft documents, supply templates, or offer anything that could be read as legal advice, so lean on your attorney or title company for the deed itself.

Recording a document costs a flat $30.00 under MCL 600.2567, as amended by PA 224 of 2016, with side charges listed below.

Statutory deed fees posted by Hillsdale County, effective October 1, 2016
Charge forPrice
Filing a deed or mortgage$30.00 total
Each extra instrument released$3.00
Treasurer's tax certificate (five descriptions)$5.00
Name search$5.00 floor, then 50 cents per year
Page of a real estate record$1.00
Certifying a copy$5.00

Lien searches at the state or federal level cost $3.00 per name, and plats copy at $2.00 per page. A transfer tax calculator is posted on the register's page for planning, with the final amount settled when the deed is presented.

Count the $500 blocks in the sale price, rounding up, and multiply the count by $4.30. That rate is 55 cents for the county, from MCL 207.504, plus $3.75 for the state, from MCL 207.525. Your closing agent will run the number and collect it with the recording fee.

  • The deed shows the price, or an affidavit does.
  • A claimed exemption is stated on the instrument.
  • Statutory exemptions: MCL 207.505 (county) and MCL 207.526 (state).
  • A land contract is exempt while title stays with the seller, and the deed that completes it must reference the contract.

A notice dated June 22, 2018 went from the register to title companies, attorneys and lenders about Public Acts 191 to 200, signed two days before. Most of the changes started on September 19, 2018, and they still shape what the office will accept.

  • A deed from a surviving owner must be backed by a certified death certificate recorded earlier, cited by liber and page, or filed alongside as a separate recording. Attaching a copy no longer meets MCL 565.48.
  • Documents signed outside Michigan follow Michigan's recording rules too, except for page layout (MCL 565.203).
  • Anything partly in a foreign language comes with an English translation (MCL 565.201).

Court orders need the clerk's certification and seal, an acknowledgment cannot omit its date, and fees are collected when a document is handed over.

The register keeps a checklist of what a deed must contain, and a deed lacking one item can be bounced. Run your draft against it before closing day.

  • Ink signatures, each with a printed name that agrees with the notary's wording (MCL 565.201).
  • A mailing address for the grantee, plus the drafter's name and business address.
  • A Michigan judge, court clerk or notary acknowledging any deed signed in the state.
  • Readable black type of 10 points or more on white 20 pound sheets, leaving 2.5 inches blank at the top of page one and half an inch elsewhere, under a line naming what the paper records.
  • Property value stated on the deed or in an attached affidavit.
  • Social Security numbers cut back to four digits.
  • Trust certificates that meet MCL 565.432 and 565.433.

Deeds signed before April 6, 2017 also had to say whether any male grantors were married or single, a rule that no longer reaches newer deeds.

The register's page offers search by full text, using optical character recognition, and by name, date, and liber and page. Tract books are linked through Kofile. An owner who wants a deed corrected should know that the office cannot change or alter a document already recorded or in the middle of recording.

Title companies do much of the research for a sale. Three operate in the city of Hillsdale: Public Title, Midstate Title and Bell Title Tri County. Ask whichever one handles your closing to confirm the transfer tax figure, since the register collects it with the recording fee.

sections.h2: What the Treasurer needs before and after closing
sections.html:
MCL 211.135 calls for a certificate from the Treasurer on any warranty deed, land contract, or land contract assignment carrying a warranty clause. Five descriptions cost $5.00, and the office answers at (517) 437-4700.

Every year the Treasurer sends a delinquent tax notice that describes the last stage of Michigan's foreclosure process. One cutoff date decides whose name is printed in a two week newspaper ad before the Show Cause Hearing in Circuit Court. A little later the office refuses partial payments and personal or business checks, taking only cash, cashier's checks, money orders and credit cards (3% convenience fee).

Anyone with an old balance should ask for a payoff before listing the house, because the deed cannot move until the certificate issues. A seller who pays the balance from closing proceeds should have the title company request the payoff figure a few days ahead.

sections.h2: A seller's checklist for the closing week
sections.html: Gather the signed deed, the Treasurer's certificate where a warranty applies, and proof of the price. Confirm with the title company whether the filing will go by e-recording or paper, since paper needs certified funds. After recording, keep the recorded copy. Hillsdale County also runs a free Property Alert service from the register that warns landowners of possible property fraud, which is worth joining if you keep other parcels. If anything looks wrong on the recorded deed, such as a misspelled name, tell your title company right away, because the register cannot alter a document once it is recorded and the fix usually means a corrective instrument at a new filing fee.

Hillsdale is the county seat and largest city, and the county is 607 square miles. The 2025 population estimate is 45,738, nearly flat since 2020. The median home value is $176,100, and owners live in 82.0% of homes, so a typical recording here is a home sale. Median rent is $832.

faqs.q: What does a Hillsdale County deed cost to file?
faqs.a: $30.00 buys the filing of a whole document. Transfer tax comes on top for a sale, and a warranty deed also needs a $5.00 certificate from the County Treasurer.

faqs.q: Can I e-record a deed in Hillsdale County?
faqs.a: Yes, through Indecomm, ePn, Simplifile or CSC/Ingeo. Payment goes by ACH, and the vendors may add fees of their own.

faqs.q: Is a personal check good for a Hillsdale County filing?
faqs.a: No. The office takes certified funds, such as a cashier's check or a money order, in its place.

faqs.q: When is the Hillsdale County register open?
faqs.a: Weekdays, from 8:30 a.m. until 5:00 p.m., in Room 212 at 33 McCollum St. Electronic filings may be sent at any hour but are handled only during those hours.

faqs.q: How is transfer tax figured on a Hillsdale County sale?
faqs.a: Round the price up to the next $500 and multiply the number of blocks by $4.30. The rate splits into $3.75 for the state and 55 cents for the county.
